extracted.intended_audience: NIH eRA Commons users (Signing Officials, Extramural Administrators, Principal Investigators, and institutional account managers)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH eRA Commons account & profile management
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and system requirements for managing user accounts, institutional profiles, personal profiles, organizational hierarchy, verifying PI support, and viewing grant application status within the NIH eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI delegate for eSNAP/X-Train
rubrics_metrics.description: PI delegate for eSNAP/ X-Train.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users with this role initially have no access other than updating their own personal profile but can be delegated PI authority to selected accounts to aid in administrative tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extramural Administrators role definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural Administrators are users with a role of SO, AA, and/or AO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Status Report (FSR) user indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial Status Report (FSR) indicates an FSR user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet-Assisted Review (IAR) user indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet-Assisted Review (IAR) indicates an IAR user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator (PI) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators (PIs) are designated by the institution to direct the project or activity being supported by the grant. The PI is responsible and accountable for the proper conduct of the project or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The role of the PI within the NIH eRA Commons is to complete the electronic grant process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO) authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing Officials (SOs) for the institution have the authority to perform legally binding grant administration actions. This includes serving as an authority responsible for submission of grant applications to the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The individual fulfilling this role can have any number of titles in the institution. The SO can create and modify accounts, and modify institution profile information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting Accounts — permission and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleting an account removes the user's affiliation at your institution from the NIH eRA Commons. Only Extramural Administrators can perform this function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Deleting an account does not remove the user's profile, nor does it remove any works-in-progress associated with the user. Procedure: Query the account; click Delete in Action column; optionally enter Comment on Delete Account Confirmation page; click Delete to confirm and return to Account List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Accounts — scope of edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural Administrators can use the Edit Account page to edit an account and modify user roles, reassign the account, or update account information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updating account information comprises changing the email address and the 'lock' status of the account. Steps: Query account list, click Edit hyperlink to open Edit Account page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassigning Accounts — procedure and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: To reassign the account to a different user: open Edit Account page, select the user name from Reassign Account drop-down, edit other info if desired, click Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page refreshes to update name, email, and role for the new user. An email is sent to the account holder of the account being edited providing a full description of changes made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Account Lock Status — meaning and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Users cannot log on to the system if their account is locked. An account is locked when a user exceeds the maximum number of tries to log on successfully or if the account is manually locked by the NIH eRA Commons system administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change lock status: open Edit Account page, in Account Lock Status field select desired lock status, edit other info if desired, click Submit. An email is sent to the account holder providing a full description of changes made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting Passwords — process and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: You can reset your password to a system-generated password. Resetting the password changes your account status from 'locked' to 'unlocked.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From main Login page click Reset Password; enter User ID and Email Address; the system sends an email with a new system-generated password to the registered email. Note: As soon as you log on with your new password you are prompted to change the password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Account Roles — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To change account roles: open Edit Account page, in Role field select the role(s) to which the account will be changed, edit other info if desired, click Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An email is sent to the account holder providing a full description of changes made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Account Email Addresses — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To change account email addresses: open Edit Account page, edit the Email field, edit other info if desired, click Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An email is sent to the account holder providing a full description of changes made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Institution Profiles — uniqueness and privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique profiles are assigned to each grantee institution. Depending on your specific privileges, you may be able to edit the institutional profile file (IPF) information or view it as read-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Basic Institution Profile Information — fields displayed
rubrics_metrics.description: View Institution Profile | Basic opens View Institution Profile page which lists institution name and contact info and the Signing Official's name, email, and phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information includes: IPF Code, Preferred Institution Name, NGA Email, Policy Announcements and Notifications Email Address, DUNS Number, Indirect Cost Negotiator, Most Recent Date of Negotiation, Human Subjects Assurance Number, Animal Welfare Assurance Number, Type of Organization, Type of Organization—Other, Ownership Control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Institution Profile Information — SO permissions and field rules
rubrics_metrics.description: SOs can edit institution profile information for their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: If a field name is followed by an asterisk (*), it is a required field. Field-specific notes: Preferred Institution Name up to 100 characters; NGA Email = email for NGAs; Policy Announcements Email = institutional notifications; DUNS Number = nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet number; Indirect Cost Negotiator 40-character maximum; Most Recent Date of Negotiation = date; Human Subjects Assurance Number 10-character max; Animal Welfare Assurance Number 10-character max; Type of Organization select from drop-down or use Other with 75-char max; Ownership Control select from drop-down. Click Submit to enter the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing IPF Assurances and Certifications — verify compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee institutions must verify that they are in compliance with specified assurances and certifications referenced in the grant application. IPF Assurances and Certifications can be viewed in read-only format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Not all assurances and certifications are applicable to each institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPF Assurances — listed assurance types
rubrics_metrics.description: List of assurances and certifications displayed for institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: ORI Certification Status, ORI Certification Date, Age Discrimination Assurance, Civil Rights Assurance, Conflict of Interest Assurance, Delinquent Debt Assurance, Drugfree Workplace Assurance, Handicapped Individuals Assurance, Institutional Debarment Assurance, Lobbying Assurance, Sex Discrimination Assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing IPF Assurances and Certifications — SO procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: SOs can edit the Institution Profile File (IPF) Assurances and Certifications for their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: Access IPF Assurances page, click Edit, select checkbox for desired assurances, and enter an explanation of the certification. For each assurance type the page requests an explanation (e.g., explain the Age Discrimination Assurance that the institution complies with prohibition of discrimination on basis of age). Click Submit; confirmation message displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Institution Usage — institution-level metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution Usage page displays a general summary of how their institution uses the NIH eRA Commons and provides detailed list at account level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage summary includes: Institution Profile Code, Institution Name, Total Number of Accounts, Total Number of Logins. Detailed usage list includes: Name, User Name, Role(s), Total Number of Logins, Last Login Date. Note: page accessible only by those with appropriate privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Organizational Hierarchy — structure and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each grantee institution is organized into a three-level organizational hierarchy: School, Division, and Department. Only institution Signing Officials are authorized to maintain this hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Division information displayed only after school selected; department only after division selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Institution Hierarchy Components — steps & selection
rubrics_metrics.description: To edit hierarchy components: open Maintain Org Hierarchy, click Edit next to school/division/department to open respective edit page, select or type desired name or pick from recommended list, select category (where applicable), click Save.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing division/department involves selecting names, optional recommended list, selecting department category, then Save to update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding New Hierarchy Components — steps
rubrics_metrics.description: To add new school/division/department: open Maintain Org Hierarchy, click New (or Create New Department), select/type new name or pick from recommended list, select category (school), click Save to update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deactivating Hierarchy Components — constraints and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hierarchy component is deactivated, it is no longer visible as part of the organizational hierarchy. Once deactivated, a component cannot be reactivated but must be added as a new component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot deactivate any school/division/department if there is an active awarded or pending application associated with it. You must first move active awarded and pending applications to another hierarchy within the same organization before deactivation. Deactivation selects next active component or blanks field if none exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Personal Profile Information — PPF sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Users with NIH eRA Commons accounts can view and update their personal profile (PPF) information. The personal profile information is divided into several sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections include: Personal Information (name, contact, DOB, SSN, citizenship, disabilities), Race/Ethnicity (five race categories, Hispanic/non-Hispanic, and options to intentionally withhold), Employment (employment history), Reviewer Address (work contact used only when user is reviewer), Residential Address, Degrees (awarded and expected), Publications (peer-reviewed publications directly relevant to proposed project with full citation text and NLM accession number). Note on addresses: three different addresses may be required for different uses (employment, reviewer, residential).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Personal Profile Information — general procedure and note
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Personal Profile | Personal Information page to edit identifying and disability information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: System Notifications field is planned for future use and is not currently active. Steps: Select Personal Profile | Personal Information, view/edit information, click Submit to enter information, select additional subsections as required for further editing. Required fields noted by asterisk (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Employment Information — process and NIH institution selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit Employment: select Personal Profile | Employments to access Employment List, click Edit for desired employer to open Employment Info page, view or edit information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selecting an NIH Recognized Institution for the employer: click Find to open Institution Selection, enter known info and Search, click Select in results to refresh Employment Info page with selected information. Click Submit to update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding New Employment Information — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Add New Employment via Personal Profile | Employments | Add New Employment to open Add New Employment page, view/edit info, use Institution Selection Find if selecting NIH Recognized Institution, click Submit to update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Degree Information — required fields and OTH handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit Degree information via Personal Profile | Degrees list and Degree Details page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: If OTH (Other) is selected for Degree Name field, Degree Text field is also required. Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*). Steps: Select Degrees, click Edit for desired degree, enter info, click Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding New Degree Information — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Add New Degree via Personal Profile | Degrees | Add New Degree to open Add New Degree page, enter degree information, click Submit to update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Publication Information — required fields and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit Publication information via Personal Profile | Publications list and Publication Details page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should list peer-reviewed publications directly relevant to the proposed project, with full citation text and the National Library of Medicine (NLM) accession number. Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*). Steps: Select Publications, click Edit, enter publication info, click Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding New Publication Information — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Add New Publication via Personal Profile | Publications | Add New Publication to open Add New Publication page, enter publication info, click Submit to update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegating/Revoking Personal Profile Edit Authority — process and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: You can delegate to and revoke authority from other NIH eRA Commons users to update your personal profile information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure to delegate: Administration | Accounts | Delegate PPF Edit, select desired users from Current Institution Users (multiple selection allowed), click Assign, confirm Save. To revoke: select users, click Revoke, confirm Save. A confirmation email is sent to the selected delegate(s) and to the email address registered with your account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifying NIH Support — when and what to verify
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH maintains PI information that includes the PI's participation in grant applications, committee involvement, and training appointments. PIs can review and edit this information when a new PI account is created (email requests verification) or at any time using Accounts tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information shown contains only the grant applications and trainee appointments that already have been awarded, and participation in Initial Review Group committees that already have convened. Procedure: open Verify NIH Support page, review information, select Correct or Incorrect for each entry (Training, Committee Involvement, Principal Investigator). To add NIH support: click Add NIH Support, enter grant number and search (Serial Number is required), click Add Grant in results to return to Verify NIH Support page updated. Add comments in Comments for NIH field and click Complete Account Request to notify NIH. For new accounts, expect notification in approximately two business days with username and randomly generated password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Grant Application Status — privileges determine scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on your privileges, you can use the Status section to get information about the status of grant proposals and Type 5 progress reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a Signing Official, you can search proposals and Type 5 progress reports for all PIs within your institution. If you are a PI, you can view only the status of your own proposals and Type 5 progress reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Grant Numbers — components
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant number provides unique identification for the grant (example: 5 R01 HL123451-01A2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant number is composed of: Type Code (application type: new, renewal, noncompeting, etc.), Activity Code (type of grant), Institute Code (IC two-letter code for NIH Institute/Center), Serial Number (unique five- or six-digit number assigned by CSR), Support Year (current year of support, e.g., 01 is new grant), Suffix Code (optional for supplements, amendments, fellowships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Querying Grant Proposals — optional fields and key filters
rubrics_metrics.description: All fields for the query information on Search Proposals page are optional. Use any desired combination of the fields to perform the account query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field notes: Budget Start Date Between (find proposals with budget start >= first date and budget end <= specified date), Grant Number (unique ID), Accession Number (identifies submitted applications prior to official grant number), Grant Status (values: Awarded, Pending, Withdrawn, Terminated, Not Funded, Returned, All), Page Size (number of records per page; default 100). Steps: enter query info, click Submit to open Proposal Search Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Proposal Search Results — result fields differ by role
rubrics_metrics.description: After running a query, view the grant proposal status information in a table format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When search performed by a PI, table provides proposal title, institution name, grant status, and status date. When performed by an extramural administrator, table provides proposal title, PI name, grant status, and budget start date. A Summary Links column may display hyperlinks to various related documents depending on grant status and user role. A hyperlinked grant number is provided next to each proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Grant Status Information — Status Information page sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Status Information page contains five sections of information for a selected grant: Status; Other Relevant Documents; Status History; Application Information; Contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status lists brief message indicating current status. Other Relevant Documents provides hyperlinks to related documentation; Status History indicates primary IC assignment and provides history of status messages with effective dates; Application Information provides Study Section and Advisory Council info and a hyperlink to roster member details; Contacts lists SRA and Program Official contact info. Procedure: from Proposal Search Results click hyperlinked grant number to open Status Information page; click hyperlinks in Other Relevant Documents to view related documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Other Relevant Documents — document types and descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Table lists various documents hyperlinked in Summary Links and Other Relevant Documents sections (examples include Abstract, Application, Fellowship Proposal Face Page, Financial Status Report (FSR), Notice of Grant Award (NGA)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract: opens grant abstract providing a brief description of the proposal covering every aspect of the project except budget. Application: if scanned opens scanned application or eSNAP PDF version of electronic Streamlined Non-competing Award Process (eSNAP) Type 5 progress report. Note: Some hyperlinks are displayed only when application status is 'Awarded' and an abstract exists. (Further document types and conditions are listed on table pages.)
